hypotheses.name: Frontier Divergence
hypotheses.statement: Persistent frontier-firm productivity gains relative to median/laggard firms tend to precede rising profit concentration and may appear before household-income divergence is obvious.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Frontier-versus-median productivity divergence adds no incremental information about subsequent profit concentration or household diffusion once aggregate productivity and cycle are controlled.
hypotheses.expected_direction: K02 widening precedes or co-moves with K03 widening; K05/K06 may lag.
hypotheses.falsifier: Repeated PIT cases in which frontier gaps widen but profit concentration does not rise, or in which aggregate-only baselines discriminate regimes equally well or better.

hypotheses.name: Winner-Less-Hiring
hypotheses.statement: As production becomes more capital/knowledge intensive, leading firms can expand output and profit without proportional employment expansion.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Leader profit/output concentration is matched proportionally by employment concentration after controlling for industry mix and cycle.
hypotheses.expected_direction: K03 widens faster than K04 employment diffusion; D-C becomes positive.
hypotheses.falsifier: In PIT replay, leader employment shares and marginal job creation rise proportionally with profit/output concentration, or K adds no discrimination beyond aggregate growth.

hypotheses.name: Asset Carrier Switch / Ownership Amplification
hypotheses.statement: When incremental household wealth increasingly depends on narrower financial/ownership assets, unequal participation can amplify wealth dispersion unless access or redistribution offsets it.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Asset-carrier composition and participation concentration do not add explanatory value for wealth divergence beyond income inequality and aggregate asset returns.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher K06 ownership concentration increases the sensitivity of wealth dispersion to asset returns.
hypotheses.falsifier: Asset ownership broadens or wealth dispersion fails to respond despite concentrated participation and strong asset returns; inequality-only baseline performs equally well.

hypotheses.name: Regional Agglomeration
hypotheses.statement: Technology-, capital-, and talent-intensive growth tends to increase spatial concentration unless mobility, housing supply, infrastructure or fiscal equalization offsets it.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Regional concentration changes are fully explained by aggregate cycle and initial regional income, with no incremental relationship to K01/K02/K03 structure.
hypotheses.expected_direction: K07 widens after persistent K01/K02 concentration unless offset by K09 mechanisms.
hypotheses.falsifier: Near-twin cases show sustained frontier concentration alongside regional catch-up, or regional K moves independently of production concentration.

hypotheses.name: Service Re-diffusion
hypotheses.statement: A sufficiently labor-absorbing service sector can compress labor/employment K even while firm/profit K remains elevated.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Service expansion does not materially reduce employment or wage dispersion once aggregate labor demand is controlled.
hypotheses.expected_direction: K04/K05 narrow while K02/K03 can remain high; candidate KR5 transition.
hypotheses.falsifier: Service absorption rises without measurable compression of employment/wage K, or apparent compression is only aggregate recession/stagnation.

hypotheses.name: Policy Slope Compression
hypotheses.statement: Predistribution institutions can alter the slope and persistence by which production K transmits into wages, household outcomes and opportunity.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: Institutional differences do not improve explanation of labor/household diffusion once production structure and aggregate cycle are controlled.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Stronger effective K09 compression weakens K02/K03 transmission into K04/K05/K08.
hypotheses.falsifier: Countries/cases with materially different institutions show indistinguishable downstream K slopes after PIT controls, or policy effects disappear under near-twin replay.

hypotheses.name: Index-Median Divergence
hypotheses.statement: High firm/profit K raises the probability that capitalization-weighted equity outcomes outperform median/equal-weight/broader-market outcomes, conditional on valuation, rates, liquidity and sector mix.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: K02/K03 state adds no incremental information about cap-weight versus broad/median relative returns after market valuation, momentum, sector and rate controls.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Higher K02/K03 is associated with narrower breadth and positive cap-weight-minus-broad/median relative return, not necessarily positive absolute index return.
hypotheses.falsifier: Japan-style or other cases repeatedly show high firm/profit K with no cap-weight relative advantage after controls; market-only baseline equals or exceeds K.

hypotheses.name: K-to-Asset Transmission
hypotheses.statement: A correctly identified K state/regime can add incremental explanatory value for selected relative asset outcomes only through an explicit value-capture, earnings, ownership and Price-Gate transmission path.
hypotheses.null_hypothesis: K state adds no out-of-sample explanatory value beyond aggregate macro and market-only baselines for relative asset outcomes.
hypotheses.expected_direction: Incremental value appears in relative breadth/concentration/value-capture outcomes before any claim about absolute return.
hypotheses.falsifier: Across preregistered PIT cases, K fails to improve relative-return/breadth discrimination or its apparent advantage disappears after valuation/rate/liquidity controls.
